title: Derived germs and pullback units on a finite geometric scheme
statement:
Fix the finite-field and finite coefficient data of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], with algebraically closed geometric field $k$ and $A=A_{E,n}$, $n\geq1$. Let $S$ be a finite $k$-scheme [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], and let $K\in D^b_c(S_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] have an explicit etale-origin witness [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness]. For $s\in S(k)$ let $K_s$ be its geometric stalk [def-weil-proetale-geometric-stalk]. The set $S(k)$ is finite, and the canonical derived germ maps give an $A$-linear isomorphism, natural in $K$,
$$\gamma_K:R\Gamma(S,K)\xrightarrow{\sim}\bigoplus_{s\in S(k)}K_s.$$
Here $R\Gamma$ is ordinary derived sections [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology]. Let $h:S\to S$ be any $k$-endomorphism and let $Lh^*$ and $Rh_*$ be the finite-level operations [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-weil-derived-direct-image]. Write
$$h^\sharp_K:R\Gamma(S,K)\longrightarrow R\Gamma(S,Lh^*K)$$
for the map induced by the unit $K\to Rh_*Lh^*K$, using the ordinary derived-sections/direct-image identification. For the canonical inverse-image stalk isomorphism $c_{h,s,K}:(Lh^*K)_s\xrightarrow{\sim}K_{h\circ s}$, induced termwise by the isomorphism of [lem-pur-proetale-inverse-image-stalk], the following equality holds in $D(A)$ for every $s\in S(k)$:
$$c_{h,s,K}\circ\operatorname{pr}_s\circ\gamma_{Lh^*K}\circ h^\sharp_K=\operatorname{pr}_{h\circ s}\circ\gamma_K.$$
Thus the unit on sections is reindexing by the map $s\mapsto h\circ s$, under the displayed germ decompositions. No invertibility of $h$ is assumed.

source.place: Step 1: finite schemes, the derived sections decomposition and the description of Phi-sharp on summands; generalized from Frobenius to any k-endomorphism

proof.text: Put $P=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and let $a:S\to P$ be the finite structure map. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula-restriction] with $f=a$ and $\bar y=\mathrm{id}_P$. Its indexing set $P(\bar y)$ is exactly $S(k)$, so this set is finite. For an etale $A$-module sheaf $F$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-strictly-henselian-sections-stalk] to the underlying abelian sheaf $a_*F$ on $P$: the field $k$ is strictly henselian because it is algebraically closed. Thus $(a_*F)(P)\to(a_*F)_{\mathrm{id}_P}$ is the germ isomorphism. By [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], $(a_*F)(P)=F(S)$. Composing with the finite-stalk restriction isomorphism gives $g_F:F(S)\xrightarrow{\sim}\prod_{s\in S(k)}F_s$. The restriction formula in the cited node sends the germ represented at $(P,\mathrm{id})$ by $u\in F(S)$ to the germ represented at $(S,s)$ by the same $u$. Hence $g_F(u)=(u_s)_s$, the specified germ map. These maps commute with sheaf maps because restriction and the stalk coprojections do. Each commutes with every constant scalar action, hence $g_F$ is $A$-linear.

The stalk functors on abelian etale sheaves are exact by [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact]. For constant-$A$ module sheaves, their kernels and cokernels have the corresponding underlying abelian kernels and cokernels by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; scalar actions on stalks are induced on germs. Thus module stalks are exact too. A finite product of exact sequences of modules is exact: its kernel is the product of the coordinate kernels, and a tuple in the product of the coordinate images has a preimage by choosing one preimage in each of the finitely many coordinates. Step 1 therefore makes $\Gamma(S_{\mathrm{et}},-)$ exact. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor], every complex computes its derived functor. Applying $g$ degreewise gives a natural isomorphism $R\Gamma(S_{\mathrm{et}},L)\cong\prod_s L_s$ for every $L\in D^+(S_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. Its components are the derived germ maps. The finite product equals the finite direct sum: the inverse to the coordinate map from the sum sends a tuple to the sum of its coordinate inclusions.

source.place: Tag 03QP and its proof, exactness of stalks and finite sums; derived exact-functor calculation

proof.text: Retain the given witness $(L,\alpha:\nu_S^*L\xrightarrow{\sim}K)$ of [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness]. The canonical derived-sections comparison of [sk-prop-sf-comparison] and the $A$-linear comparison-stalk isomorphisms of [lem-cbc-proetale-comparison-stalk] identify the source and target of the pro-etale germ map with those of Step 2. We check that the maps agree. The scheme $S$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-field-affine-finite-dim]. The sections formula of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-sections], at the constant presentation $S=S$, sends an etale global section $u$ to its comparison inverse-image section. Taking its germ at $s$ and applying the comparison-stalk map returns $[S,s,u]$, since the comparison morphism is inclusion of etale neighbourhoods [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. This is precisely the etale germ of $u$. For complexes choose a bounded-below injective representative $I$ of $L$ by [lem-sc-bounded-below-injective-resolution]. The pro-etale module-sheaf category is Grothendieck by [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian]. Its terms have exact etale sections by Step 2, and their comparison inverse images are pro-etale-sections-acyclic by the derived-sections comparison applied to $I^r[0]$. The complexes clause of [lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity] consequently computes pro-etale derived sections on $\nu_S^*I$ by termwise sections. Stalks compute termwise by [lem-cbc-proetale-classical-stalk]. The preceding germ equation is now an equality of chain maps, so it remains an equality after localization. Transport through $\alpha$ proves that the canonical $\gamma_K$ is the $A$-linear isomorphism of Step 2; it is natural in $K$, since full faithfulness in [sk-prop-sf-comparison] lifts every morphism between witness realizations. Here [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] and [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology] interpret ordinary sections as the same module-valued derived sections, since point evaluation is exact.

source.place: Tags 099V, 099W (lemma-relative-comparison, lemma-compare-cohomology), 0993 (lemma-classical-point); comparison on section representatives

proof.text: The argument so far applies to every bounded-below etale-origin $A$-complex, without any constructibility or Tor-amplitude assumption. In particular it applies to $Lh^*K$. Indeed [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] identifies $h^{-1}\nu_S^*L$ with $\nu_S^*h_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}L$. Finite-level pullback is termwise exact inverse image by [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]; the etale inverse image is also exact by [lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-exact], with its constant coefficient action. Applying these functors to the witness gives the required bounded-below etale-origin witness for $Lh^*K$. Thus both germ decompositions occurring in the claimed equation exist. The inverse-image stalk isomorphism of [lem-pur-proetale-inverse-image-stalk] is $A$-linear, since its germ construction commutes with each constant scalar operation. Exactness of the stalk from [lem-cbc-proetale-classical-stalk] gives its termwise derived version $c_{h,s,K}$.

source.place: Tag 09A5, morphisms of pro-etale sites; comparison pullback and Tag 0993

proof.text: We calculate the unit on an arbitrary pro-etale $A$-module sheaf $M$. Write $v_M:\Gamma(S,M)\to\Gamma(S,h^{-1}M)$ for its sections map. In the inverse-image colimit of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], its value at a section $u$ is the coprojection indexed by the final target object $V=S$ and the identity $S\to S\times_{S,h}S\cong S$, followed by sheafification. To normalize the canonical $c_{h,s,M}$ of [lem-pur-proetale-inverse-image-stalk], use [lem-cbc-proetale-sheafification-geometric-stalk] to calculate before sheafification. A representative is $b\in M(V)$, a pointed neighbourhood $(U,t)$ of $s$ and a map $\theta:U\to S\times_{S,h}V$. Send it to $[V,\operatorname{pr}_V\theta t,b]\in M_{hs}$. Restriction along an arrow gives the same colimit class, so this defines the comparison. Its inverse sends $[V,w,b]$ to the inverse-image coprojection on $S\times_{S,h}V$ at the lift $(s,w)$. One composite fixes $[V,w,b]$; the other fixes the original class because restriction of that coprojection along $\theta$ is exactly the original representative. This is the canonical inverse-image stalk identification, with both maps retaining the represented section. For the representative of $v_M(u)$ just described its value is $[S,hs,u]$. Consequently $c_{h,s,M}\,\operatorname{germ}_s\,v_M=\operatorname{germ}_{hs}$. All maps here are $A$-linear and natural in $M$.

source.place: Tag 09A5, section-morphism; Tag 0993, lemma-classical-point; explicit inverse-image and stalk colimits

proof.text:
By [lem-sc-bounded-below-injective-resolution], choose a bounded-below injective K-injective representative $I$ of $K$ and such a resolution $q:h^*I\to J$. Use the constant-ring identification to write $h^*I=h^{-1}I$. In the derived adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], the unit at $I$ is represented by $I\xrightarrow{\eta_I}h_*h^*I\xrightarrow{h_*q}h_*J$: its adjunct is $q$, which represents the identity of $Lh^*K$. Ordinary derived sections [def-weil-derived-direct-image, def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] and the direct-image formula of [def-weil-proetale-module-direct-image] therefore represent $h^\sharp_K$ by $\Gamma(I)\xrightarrow{v_I}\Gamma(h^*I)\xrightarrow{\Gamma(q)}\Gamma(J)$. Indeed $h_*J$ is K-injective, as follows directly from the adjunction: homotopies of maps from an acyclic $B$ into $h_*J$ are homotopies of maps from the acyclic $h^*B$ into $J$, since $h^*$ is exact. The derived germ maps are represented by the termwise germs of $I$ and $J$, since stalks are exact [lem-cbc-proetale-classical-stalk]. Naturality of germs gives $\operatorname{germ}_s\Gamma(q)=q_s\operatorname{germ}_s$, and $q_s$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The stalk comparison on the target represented by $J_s$ is $c_{h,s,I}q_s^{-1}$. Substitution gives, in $D(A)$,
$$c_{h,s,I}q_s^{-1}\operatorname{germ}_s\Gamma(q)v_I=c_{h,s,I}\operatorname{germ}_s v_I=\operatorname{germ}_{hs},$$
the last equality being Step 5 degreewise. In the decompositions of Steps 1-4 this is exactly the asserted equation with $\operatorname{pr}_s$ and $\operatorname{pr}_{hs}$. It holds for every $s$, with no use of injectivity or surjectivity of $s\mapsto hs$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q97-ca8f5f1a3 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all six steps, the full statements of all 27 cited nodes, the proof of lem-pur-proetale-inverse-image-stalk, the parent's Step 1a, unit step 1, main-20261015 Step 1, and Stacks 03QP/03QO, 0993 and its warning, 099V/099W, 09A5 and 03D3 (labels match tags). There are no new nodes and the statement is unchanged; the coefficients are finite-level A_{E,n} on S_proet, and the étale-origin witness is required, which is needed because of the 0993 warning. Step 1: the finite stalk formula with f=a, ybar=id gives P(ybar)=S(k); k is strictly henselian, so sections equal the stalk; the composite is u -> (u_s). Step 2: Γ(S_et,-) is a finite product of exact stalk functors, so every complex computes RΓ. Step 3: through the witness, comparison-sections at the constant presentation and comparison-stalk make the pro-étale germ map on ν*I a termwise isomorphism; Leray clause 3 hypotheses hold. Step 4: comparison-pullback gives Lh*K a bounded-below witness, without needing constructibility. Step 5: the explicit map and its inverse are exactly a_F t_F^{-1} of the inverse-image-stalk lemma's proof (checked line by line); pr_V φ(s) = h∘s. Step 6: by the characterization on representatives in lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general, the unit is (h_*q)η_I; h_*J is K-injective, and cancelling q_s gives equality in D(A). Small cases checked: S empty, Spec k, k[e]/e^2 with e->0, two points with swap, two points with constant h, K=0. No duplicate among zero-dimensional-sections-stalks, the derived global germ nodes, or the étale inverse-image-stalk-germ node. No cycle and no SGA. All declared tool uses lie on the transitive route of sk-thm-trace-formula; I accept them. No changes.
